walkthrough:
Identify the structure of $y = |4x - 2|$:
This is a V-shaped graph with vertex on the $x$-axis where $4x - 2 = 0$, giving $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Determine the key points:
The vertex is at $(0.5, 0)$.
The $y$-intercept occurs at $x = 0$ where $y = |-2| = 2$, giving $(0, 2)$.
At $x = 1$, $y = |4(1) - 2| = 2$, giving $(1, 2)$.

Draw the graph:
Sketch two straight rays meeting at $(0.5, 0)$: one ray with gradient $4$ for $x \geqslant 0.5$, and one ray with gradient $-4$ for $x < 0.5$, ensuring axis scales and labels are clearly shown.

walkthrough: Find the critical values where the line $y = 1 + 3x$ intersects the two branches of $y = |4x - 2|$:

Solve for the positive branch where $4x - 2 > 0$ ($x > 0.5$):
$$1 + 3x = 4x - 2$$
$$4x - 3x = 1 + 2 \implies x = 3$$

Solve for the negative branch where $4x - 2 < 0$ ($x < 0.5$):
$$1 + 3x = -(4x - 2)$$
$$1 + 3x = 2 - 4x$$
$$7x = 1 \implies x = \dfrac{1}{7}$$

Test intervals to satisfy $1 + 3x < |4x - 2|$:
For $x = 0$ ($x < 1/7$): $1 < |-2| = 2$, which is true.
For $x = 1$ ($1/7 < x < 3$): $4 < |2| = 2$, which is false.
For $x = 4$ ($x > 3$): $13 < |14| = 14$, which is true.

State the solution set using strict inequalities:
$$x < \dfrac{1}{7} \quad \text{or} \quad x > 3$$
